properties.foundation_analysis: Bedrock comprises Carboniferous sedimentary strata of the Lothian Oil-Shale Group, interleaved with basaltic volcanic sills. Superficial deposits consist of dense Quaternary glacial till. Building fabric utilizes indigenous pale-buff to blonde Craigleith and Hailes sandstones, bedded in non-hydraulic lime and crushed stone mortars. Ground drainage follows engineered historic subterranean storm sewers along the ridge profile.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Perimeter of Charlotte Square Gardens populated by mature *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime), and *Ulmus glabra* (Wych Elm). Late-September phenology displays dense, mature canopies exhibiting early autumn senescence: partial chlorophyll loss, mottled yellowing leaf margins, and scattered crown thinning without major defoliation.

properties.architectural_summary: Neoclassical Edinburgh New Town palatial urban block designed by Robert Adam and executed by Robert Reid. Central visual anchor features West Register House with its monumental portico, colossal attached columns, and elevated copper-clad dome drum. Flanking symmetrical three-storey and attic terraced townhouses over rusticated basements. Planar facades rectified to strict plumb verticals; fenestration follows regular grids of timber sash-and-case windows (six-over-six and twelve-over-twelve configurations) with continuous stringcourses and projecting eaves cornices.
